name: list_cases
description: List the OpenFOAM cases in the run directory ($FOAM_RUN). A case kept in a container folder is listed as container/case: pass that whole name wherever a case is asked for.

name: case_info
description: Summary of one case: directories, time steps, whether it has a mesh.

case.description: Case name, as listed by list_cases (container/case for a case in a container)

name: list_case_files
description: List files and directories inside a case. Omit path for the case root.

name: read_case_file
description: Read one file from a case, e.g. 0/U or system/controlDict. Returns at most 256 KB: for a larger file it says the size and shows its first 4 KB. Never use it for logs, fields in time directories, constant/polyMesh or postProcessing — the digest tools read those in WSL and return a short summary.

name: write_case_file
description: Write one complete file in a case, creating parent directories as needed. Confined to the run directory. OpenFOAM dictionary names and syntax are validated automatically and a known-invalid write is refused; use validate_case_files afterwards for cross-file checks.

name: run_openfoam
description: Run one OpenFOAM executable inside a case (blockMesh, checkMesh, foamRun, snappyHexMesh, decomposePar, Allrun, …). Only guarded commands this installation exposes are accepted; application option names and required values are checked against that binary's own -help, and shell syntax is refused. For a parallel run write exactly "mpirun -np <n> <command> -parallel". Use background: true for long solves instead of a trailing "&". Returns the exit code and the last lines of output.
unrestrictedDescription: Run a command inside a case directory, in WSL. UNRESTRICTED MODE is on: this is a real shell — any command, pipes, redirects and chaining all work. The one thing still refused is the Windows disk: paths under /mnt/ are out of bounds, because that is the user's own documents and this application's files, and no OpenFOAM work needs them. Everything inside WSL is yours. Say what you are about to run before running anything destructive. Use background: true for long solves. Returns the exit code and the last lines of output.

name: validate_case_files
description: Check a related set of files against THIS OpenFOAM installation: every type/model/solver name against the run-time selection tables, and syntax through OpenFOAM's own parser. write_case_file already validates each individual dictionary; use this before running for the complete changed set.

name: foam_lookup
description: Ask the installation what is valid. With "name": whether that type exists here, which tables it belongs to, and which dictionary keys it accepts. With "kind": the whole list (solvers, scalarBCs, vectorBCs, functionObjects, fvModels, fvConstraints, applications). This is ground truth for the installed version — prefer it over recollection.

name: foam_help
description: What a command or type actually IS on this installation, and where the answer came from. Looks in three places in order: the installation index, then the command's own -help run in WSL, then the web - the last only if the first two found nothing (or if web:true forces it). Every finding is labelled with its source. USE THIS instead of recalling what an option does: your memory of OpenFOAM is dominated by older versions and by the ESI fork, and this reads the binaries on the user's disk. Whatever you take from it, tell the user where it came from.

name.description: A command or type name, e.g. snappyHexMesh

question.description: What you want to know, for the web query if it comes to that

web.description: Search the web even if the installation answered

name: search_tutorials
description: Find the closest real examples in the tutorials shipped with this installation. Useful for "how is this normally written".

name: analyze_log
description: Digest of a solver log, computed in WSL in one streaming pass whatever its size: whether the run finished, crashed (FOAM FATAL, signal) or is still running; time steps and time reached; initial residual per field (first/last/min/max and a history of evenly spaced steps); linear-solver iterations; continuity errors; Courant number; deltaT; outer-loop convergence; bounding; warnings; and the last lines when it did not end. Omit log to take the newest log that holds residuals. Read-only.

case.description: Case name, as listed by list_cases (container/case for a case in a container)

log.description: e.g. "foamRun", "log.foamRun", "snappyHexMesh"; omit for the newest solver log

name: read_log_excerpt
description: A bounded slice of a log (at most 120 lines): around the first or last occurrence of a literal text (match), from a line number (line + count), or the last lines (tail). Use it to look at a place analyze_log pointed to — a warning, the step where residuals jumped ("Time = 0.0123s"), the error. Read-only.

case.description: Case name, as listed by list_cases (container/case for a case in a container)

match.description: Literal text to find, not a regular expression

context.description: Lines before and after the match (default 15, at most 60)

name: analyze_fields
description: Digest of the time directories, computed in WSL without transferring the fields: which times exist at the case root and in the processor directories of a decomposed case (and whether they agree or were reconstructed), then for one time (default: the latest anywhere) every volume field's min, max and mean — vectors as magnitude and components — combined over all processors, with NaN and physically impossible values flagged, and the boundary condition types per patch. Face/point fields (phi, Uf) only when named in fields. Read-only.

case.description: Case name, as listed by list_cases (container/case for a case in a container)

time.description: Time directory name, e.g. "0.5"; omit or "latest" for the latest

name: postprocess_summary
description: Digest of postProcessing/: for every tabular function-object output (forces, coefficients, field values, probes, residuals, sampled lines) the rows and time span, and per column the last value, range, mean over the final fifth and drift between the last two fifths — small drift means the quantity has settled. Restarts are stitched. Surfaces and VTK are not read. Read-only.

case.description: Case name, as listed by list_cases (container/case for a case in a container)

name: mesh_summary
description: Digest of the mesh without reading points/faces/owner/neighbour: cells, points and faces from the file headers, bounding box, patches with types and face counts (2D/axisymmetric detection), zones, sets, meshes kept in time directories (snappyHexMesh without -overwrite, moving meshes), the decomposition (cells per processor, imbalance, processor interface faces) and whether the 0/ boundary conditions cover the patches. With quality: true it also runs checkMesh (-latestTime when the mesh is in a time directory) and reports every failed or warned check; checkMesh writes the failing cells into polyMesh/sets, nothing else.

case.description: Case name, as listed by list_cases (container/case for a case in a container)
